ticket.title: miter index --dirty at the suite root cannot see changes in member repositories
acceptance_criteria:
DONE 2026-11-06, commit 6ccfc70 (miter). The per-file baseline is persisted, which was the missing prerequisite under GB-301, GB-302 and GB-237.

THE ROOT CAUSE, restated because it is one defect and I had previously described three. A full `miter index` wrote symbols and references and never wrote the per-file ledger. set_indexed_file was called from exactly two places, both of them the incremental passes themselves, and save_redb deletes and rebuilds the database from the engine - so any ledger an incremental run did write was erased by the next full index. An index consequently had no memory of its own files.

WHAT CHANGED:
  Engine carries relative path -> IndexedFileRecord (digest, size, mtime).
  The polyglot pass fills it from bytes it already read, so neither the digest nor the mtime costs an extra pass.
  save_redb writes it back through a second handle after the exclusive one is dropped, because redb refuses two handles.
  WorkspaceStore::set_baseline writes the hash table and the record table in ONE transaction - the first attempt did two commits per file and turned a ten-second index into more than thirty, which is a worse regression than the emptiness it fixed.

MEASURED at the suite root, editing a file inside miter/ (a separate repository the root .gitignore excludes):
  before  dirty-indexed: 0 symbols from 0 files (0 skipped, 0 scanned)       0.60 s
  after   dirty-indexed: 5 symbols from 1 files (957 skipped, 959 scanned)   1.20 s

That is GB-301 fixed as a consequence: the edit is found by mtime cross-reference over the baseline, not by git, so it works at any repository depth and no longer depends on which repository happens to contain the caller.

NO ROWS LOST, which was the acceptance clause that mattered: two consecutive full indexes both report 7362 symbols and 14069 universal. A skip mechanism that quietly dropped symbols would have been a worse bug than the one being fixed.

NOT yet done, and now cheap: the polyglot pass still re-parses unchanged files during a FULL index, because it does not consult the baseline it now writes. That is the remaining half of GB-302 and the reason a full index is still ~10 s. GB-237's auto-index can now be built on a mechanism that detects staleness correctly, but should wait for the skip so a refresh costs a second rather than ten.

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, 280 tests green, audit clean after splitting store/mod.rs (256 lines) into store/ledger.rs.

task.title: miter index --dirty at the suite root cannot see changes in member repositories

acceptance_criteria:
REPRODUCED 2026-11-06.

  cd <suite root>; append a line to miter/src/cli/impact.rs; miter index . --dirty
  -> 'dirty-indexed: 0 symbols from 0 files (0 skipped, 0 scanned)'  in 0.60 s

  cd miter; append the same line; miter index . --dirty --db .gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb
  -> 'dirty-indexed: 5 symbols from 1 files (0 skipped, 1 scanned)'  in 1.00 s

The edit is invisible from the root because --dirty asks git for the repository containing the path, and miter/ is its own repository that the root .gitignore excludes. So the command reports success and zero work.

This is the exact failure mode this session kept finding: a check that cannot see what it is asked about reports clean. The concrete consequence is that auto-index built on this would claim the index is current after every edit in every member repository.

Preferred fix is not 'walk the repositories' but 'stop asking git': the file-hash ledger (GB-302) answers the same question per file, is repository-agnostic, and is already the mechanism the tracked pass uses. Fixing GB-302 first may retire this ticket rather than duplicate the machinery.

ROOT CAUSE 2026-11-06, and it is one defect behind two tickets. My earlier diagnoses on both were incomplete.

What I said first: GB-302 was 'the polyglot pass ignores the hash ledger' and GB-301 was '--dirty asks git and git cannot see member repositories'. Both are true statements about individual mechanisms. Neither is the reason the incremental machinery does nothing.

The actual defect: `miter index` (the full path) writes symbols and references and NOT the incremental ledgers. set_indexed_file is called from exactly two places in the tree - analysis/dirty/ingest.rs and ingest/tracked.rs - both of which are the incremental paths themselves. A full index therefore produces an index whose per-file baseline is empty, and every incremental mechanism afterwards is inert:
  - detect_dirty_files iterates indexed_files to compare size and mtime. Empty set, zero comparisons, zero dirty files.
  - the same emptiness makes --dirty report 'files_scanned: 0, files_skipped: 0', which reads as 'nothing to do' rather than 'nothing can be determined'.
  - file_hash_count is likewise only ever populated by the incremental paths, so the hash-based skip never has a digest to compare against.

Evidence chain, all measured:
  miter index .            -> 958/958 files, 10.2 s, then
  edit miter/src/cli/impact.rs
  miter index . --dirty    -> 0 files scanned, 0 skipped, 0.60 s   (suite root)
  same edit, run inside miter/ -> 1 file, 5 symbols, 1.00 s        (git sees it here)
The second result is the tell: inside the member repository the git fast path finds the file even though the ledger is empty. At the suite root the git path sees nothing because the root repository excludes the member directories, and the mtime path sees nothing because the ledger is empty. Two independent reasons for the same wrong answer, both silent.

Consequence for GB-237: auto-index cannot be built before this is fixed, and the fix is not 'skip files', it is 'write the baseline'. The order is: full index records hash + size + mtime per file and persists them; then the mtime path works at any repository depth without git; then auto-index is a policy over a working mechanism.

Shape of the fix, for whoever takes it:
  1. Engine holds per-file (relative path, digest, size, mtime) gathered during ingest - it already reads and hashes every file in the tracked pass, so the data is nearly free.
  2. persist::save_redb writes those rows alongside the symbols, so one full index leaves a complete baseline.
  3. Then the polyglot skip (GB-302) becomes a one-line lookup, and dirty detection (GB-301) becomes ledger-based, which drops its dependence on git and on the containing repository.

The lesson, since this is the third multi-repository blind spot this session (GB-293 telemetry, then this): a mechanism that is correct per repository composes into a suite that reports success while measuring nothing. The suite is twelve repositories and almost every one of its instruments is written as if it were one.
